reason: WBA's only English league title was 1919-20 (First Division), with then-record 104 goals and 60 points. Hint stats confirmed by multiple sources.
WBA won the 1954 FA Cup and finished league runners-up that season; Wolves won their first-ever league title in 1953-54, denying WBA the double. Both stem claims verified.

1966 League Cup Final (last two-legged final) confirmed: West Ham won leg one 2-1, WBA won leg two 4-1 at The Hawthorns, 5-3 on aggregate to Albion. Hint detail ("hit four at The Hawthorns") matches the 4-1 scoreline exactly.
Ron Atkinson left Cambridge United (Fourth Division champions 1976-77) to become WBA manager in January 1978, and soon signed his former captain Brendon Batson from Cambridge.
Tony 'Bomber' Brown holds both WBA all-time records: 720 appearances and 279 goals (1963-1980), confirmed by club and independent sources.
Willie Johnston (Scotland) failed a drugs test at the 1978 World Cup after the Peru match and was sent home from Argentina; well-documented fact.
Manchester United 3-5 WBA at Old Trafford on 30 December 1978, 3-3 at half-time, widely regarded as one of English football's greatest matches. Matches hint exactly.
As FA Cup holders, WBA entered the 1968-69 Cup Winners' Cup and lost to Dunfermline Athletic in the quarter-finals (0-0 away, 0-1 home); Dunfermline went on to the semis, matching the hint.
